sections.heading: Planning your Duet @ Emily interior
sections.text:
In a boutique District 9 building, every centimetre of the plan tends to matter. There is less room to hide a messy entry, a loose wardrobe or a kitchen that looks temporary, and the finish is often judged at close range. That is a natural brief for Maison. We design built-in carpentry — an entry cabinet, a living-room joinery wall, a fitted kitchen, and full-height wardrobes, including a headboard wall if the bedroom plan allows it — and we photograph the work the way a professional interior is seen: tight junctions, consistent grain, and closer shots of materials, not only a wide show-flat angle. We do not use IKEA-style flat-pack furniture as the backbone of the home.

No official floor plan is on file, so typologies, room sizes and a sample layout are not published here, and we will not invent a typical Duet @ Emily plan. River Modern, One Leonie Residences, Orchard Sophia and CanningHill Piers are other Maison pages in or next to this district. Use them as nearby links. Do not assume they share a layout, a tenure or a management handbook with this building. City or river views should be checked from your own stack and floor; we will not promise an outlook.

Once keys are in sight, inspect defects, measure, and obtain the management corporation’s approval before fabrication. In a small building, access, working hours and protection of common areas can be stricter, so read the rules early. A moderate carpentry scope is often planned at six to ten weeks on site after approvals; that is an editorial allowance, not a guarantee. WhatsApp Maison with your approved plan when you have it.
